goal: A validate_task(task, *, repo_root) -> list of defects, exported from flywheel_core, statically flags a command grader whose run is empty or not shell-parseable and a command grader whose run references a repo-relative path that does not exist, while a task whose graders all parse and whose referenced paths all exist returns no defects -- without executing any grader and without dragging IO into the pure task module.

relevant: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/task.py -- the Task/Grader/CommandGrader dataclasses (PURE; no IO). Do NOT add filesystem/shell logic here (test_task_module_purity.py enforces it).

packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/loaders.py -- the IO-permitted boundary; validate_task (filesystem path-existence + bash -n shell-parse) belongs here or in a sibling validation module, NOT in task.py
packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/__init__.py -- export validate_task (and the defect record type) from flywheel_core so the verb and the orchestrator consume one shape (spec shared invariant)
docs/task-schema.md -- the existing Task/Grader schema rules already enforced at construction; this adds checks on top, it does not replace them
references: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/task.py -- CommandGrader.run is the field validate_task inspects; iterate task.graders and check only command graders

subprocess.run(['bash', '-n', '-c', run]) is the shell-parse check (exit non-zero => unparseable); a path token is a run argument containing '/', not starting with '-', without '://', with trailing '/' and a trailing '/*' glob segment stripped, resolved under repo_root (spec D-2)
constraints: validate_task is STATIC -- it must NOT execute any grader command (D-1). Shell-parse uses `bash -n` (parse only, no run); path-existence is a filesystem stat. Never run the grader's `run`.

Signature is fixed: validate_task(task, *, repo_root: Path) -> list[<defect>] where each defect carries the owning task id and a human-readable detail naming the specific problem (the empty path or the parse error). Export both validate_task and the defect type from flywheel_core.
Only `command` graders gain the new shell/path checks; transcript/rubric/manual graders are validated only by their existing schema rules (out of scope to re-check).

Keep flywheel_core.task and flywheel_core.lifecycle pure -- no json/pathlib/io/subprocess in those modules. The path/shell checks live in the loader/validation module (must-not-regress; task-module-purity grader).

The path-token heuristic is conservative (D-2): only tokens that look like intended repo-relative paths are existence-checked; flags, URLs, and bare words are never flagged (no false positives on a valid task).
Commit with a clear conventional-commit message; no emojis.
Run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not author, edit, weaken, delete, or read anything under .flywheel/holdout/00034-task-definition-validation/ -- the held-out oracle is the grading surface.
Do not execute graders or add any dry-run-against-base mode (D-1).
Do not attempt to catch tool-semantic errors in a command that parses and runs (e.g. wrong CLI flags) -- explicitly out of scope.
Do not weaken the existing Task/Grader schema validation or the purity tests.
Do not add the CLI verb or the schedule-time dispatch refusal here -- that is the dependent task (validate-verb-and-dispatch).
edge_cases: A run referencing an existing path (e.g. packages/flywheel-core/tests) yields NO defect; a run referencing .flywheel/holdout/does-not-exist/ yields a defect naming the missing path (criterion 1).
An empty run and an unterminated shell construct (e.g. 'for f in') each yield a parse/empty defect; a well-formed multi-token run does not (criterion 2).
A run with only flags and a tool name (no path tokens) is valid; a URL argument (https://...) is never flagged as a missing path.
A glob target (e.g. packages/**/tests) whose literal prefix exists is not flagged; only a token resolving to a concrete non-existent location is.
notes: Held-out oracle under .flywheel/holdout/00034-task-definition-validation/ feeds validate_task a mixed corpus of valid and invalid task definitions and asserts the exact valid/invalid split + defect contents. Authored out-of-band; outside pytest testpaths; collected explicitly by the grader.
This is the validation layer; the verb + schedule-time refusal depend on it (spec Decomposition Hint).
